patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 5's changed support interfaces now both reference SUPPORT_REACTION, matching their support/reaction meaning rather than active-side PRIMARY_THRUST or PARKING_THRUST. Main physical elements and paths align with claim 1 and the read description passages: axially sliding disc/mounting, opposite pads and axial engagement, piston/collar primary thrust, lever mounting/straddling, and independent thrust paths.

functional_completeness.rationale: The concept captures the central architecture: two independent actuators apply to the same active pad, sliding disc axial motion engages the passive pad against fixed support, and primary hydraulic input is represented. Patent-supported alternative wear adjustment is disclosed in warnings and not incorrectly treated as mandatory.

flow_consistency.rationale: Both primary_mount_to_caliper_support and lever_pivot_to_caliper_support now use SUPPORT_REACTION with mechanical_force ports; the two active-pad thrust paths remain separate, and axial_disc_motion connects compatible mechanical_linear ports. Flow roles and directions are coherent.

claim_traceability.rationale: No requirements have been invented, claim 1's previously unsupported one-sector requirement is absent, and the represented independent paths and symmetry/lever structure correspond to the cited claims and passages. Citations cover modeled ID-bearing items in the supplied candidate.

interfaces.rationale: Revision 5 addresses both prior support-interface mismatches. Mating subsystem IDs and port IDs resolve, flow types match both endpoint ports and interface types, and each connection is recorded once. The defined PRIMARY_THRUST and PARKING_THRUST remain on their active-pad output paths.

textbook_application.rationale: Textbook material is used only for modeling guidance; candidate facts derive from patent passages. No executable constraints or unsupported requirements are introduced. The model uses physical components rather than function-name pseudo-subsystems.

summary: Independently reviewed saved SJS revision 5. The prior findings are addressed: both primary actuator mount-to-caliper and lever pivot-to-caliper support interfaces now reference SUPPORT_REACTION, while active thrust flows remain assigned to the active-pad interfaces. Axial disc motion, port compatibility, source/sink representation, model scope, patent grounding, claim traceability, and the stated alternative wear-adjustment omission are coherent. No unresolved issues identified; this review does not edit the candidate.
